alex: Running a 10k qps replay vs synthetic mix and seeing a weird tail when JSON-mode + tool-calls enabled. p95 jumps ~2.5x. anyone dug into kernel selection or batching assumptions there?
maya: interesting — is this with KV cache warm or cold?
ajex: kv was mostly warm for the replay, ~90% hits. i saw the extra latency only when structured output validation was on.
alex: repro snippet: `replay-harness --trace -m my-open-model --mode=replay --json-validation=on --qps=10000`
replay-bot: started replay at 1767456792 for run id r-2026-03-01-01
tj: can you paste the trace where p95 spikes? small chunks are easiest to scan.
alex: paste: ```
[PROFILE] batch_size=16 kernel=matmul_opt_v2 latency=12.4ms
[PROFILE] batch_size=16 kernel=matmul_fallback latency=37.9ms
[PROFILE] json-validate time_ms=21.3 retries=1
[PROFILE] kv-lookup hit=true time_ms=0.9
```
maya: that kernel fallback is suspicious — fallback path has scalar loops that blow up at higher seq len. what's the seq_len distribution?
alex: replay has mix: 60% short (<64), 30% medium (128-256), 10% long (>512). when structured on, validator often forces streaming vs non-streaming path? so batching behavior changes.
sam: i remember a perf regression pr that touched the kernel selection heuristic — 1729-kernel-selector-change. maybe related. it changed threshold to favor conservative kernels for safety with token types.
jin: linked perf regression had unit tests but not replay coverage for JSON-toolcall workload. we should run apple-to-apple: synthetic vs replay with identical token distribution and toolcall frequency.
tj: agree. action items: 1) reproduce minimal case that toggles kernel selection, 2) add replay harness scenario to CI, 3) measure validation cost separately.
alex: did a quick isolate: disabling JSON schema validation drops the extra 20ms, but replay shows more retries on tool-calls (validation used to catch structure earlier). tradeoff.
maya: maybe move validation off critical path: async validate + best-effort fallback with TTL cache for validated schemas. that would keep latency low and still catch bad outputs.
sam: can we add a shadow validator that runs outside SLO to gather stats first? then promote if safe.
jin: also want to see if batching heuristic treats validation as blocking token emission. maybe we can let validators operate on completed chunks while runtime streams tokens.
deploy-bot: canary deployed build r-2026-03-01-kvfix to production subset (10%) at 1767456840
alex: summary of experiments so far: 1) JSON validation on -> p95 up by 2.5x, more kernel fallbacks seen. 2) validation off -> lower p95, but +0.8% invalid outputs observed in replay. 3) KV cache hit rate unaffected.
tj: next steps: create a replay job that toggles only validator (on/off), collects kernel selection histogram, batch sizes, and toolcall retry counts. file a perf task and assign to eng-runtime.
alex: creating task now and attaching replay config. will post job id when ready. :thumbsup:
